title: Evaluating the Efficacy of LLM-Based Reasoning for Multiobjective HPC Job Scheduling
problem: HPC job scheduling must balance multiple conflicting objectives (makespan, wait time, resource utilization, fairness). Traditional methods (FCFS, SJF) and optimization techniques fail to adapt to dynamic workloads or simultaneously optimize multiple objectives.
motivation: Current HPC schedulers use static, often single-objective heuristics. Modern LLMs with reasoning capabilities (chain-of-thought, ReAct) offer alternative approach: interpretable decision-making via natural language, scratchpad memory for history tracking, and constraint satisfaction.
method: LLM-based scheduler using ReAct framework (Reason + Act): 1) Scratchpad memory tracking scheduling history, 2) Natural-language feedback for decision refinement, 3) Constraint enforcement module ensuring feasibility. Evaluation on real-world HPC workloads (7 scenarios: heterogeneous, bursty, adversarial) using OpenAI O4-Mini and Anthropic Claude 3.7. Comparison vs FCFS, SJF, Google OR-Tools on 10-100 job instances.
key_novelty: First comprehensive study of reasoning-capable LLMs (ReAct framework) for multiobjective HPC scheduling with natural-language interpretability.
contributions: LLM-based ReAct scheduler for HPC job scheduling
Scratchpad memory mechanism for scheduling history tracking
Evaluation on 7 real-world HPC workload scenarios
Comparative analysis vs traditional and optimization-based methods
Analysis of reasoning quality vs computational overhead tradeoff

metrics.objectives: Makespan, wait time, resource utilization, fairness
metrics.focus: Constraint satisfaction, multiobjective tradeoff, workload adaptability

findings.strength: Balances multiple objectives effectively; transparent reasoning via natural language
findings.adaptation: Handles diverse workloads without domain-specific training
findings.limitation: Tradeoff between reasoning quality and computational overhead; not real-time ready

limitations: Abstract only - no specific performance metrics, no latency data, limited to small job counts (10-100); real deployments 1000s+ jobs
primary_theme: LLM-based reasoning for complex system optimization
